This is Google's explanation of how sitelinks work. I have worked for companies that tailor how Google returns your search results; we gave direct feedback to Google (and Bing for that matter) in regards to how the search algorithm should function. Said feedback is independent of any one particular site and instead dealt with things like the relevancy of search results (e.g. a search for voat.co shouldn't bring up voat.com, despite the URLs being so similar).

To very basically explain how this works: Google's algorithm assigns a certain rating to the search results for any given query; this rating is then "crowdsourced" through a regimented testing process to see if the algorithm falls in line with user opinion on how useful the results are. Google takes the test results and uses it to tweak their algorithm accordingly. This is very nebulously referred to by the line "Google doesn't guarantee that demoted URLs will never appear as a sitelink, but we do consider a demotion a strong hint that we'll try to honor when generating sitelinks."

It is pretty unlikely that FPH should rank above News, Technology, Science, Gaming, TIL, et cetera, and it is outright mystifying that /v/niggers is even remotely close to its current priority in the search results given their respective subscriber counts (if nothing else).
